diagnosis.root_cause: The OLT health check is falsely reporting all PONs as failed because the PON/ONU OID subtree does not respond, while the OLT itself remains reachable and operational. This is a monitoring or SNMP-subtree polling defect, not an OLT or PON outage.
evidence: The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, so this is not an OLT failure.
The OLT CPU, memory, temperature, uptime, and historical telemetry are healthy.
Every ONU probe on EPON0/2 returns responds:false rather than online:0; this means the probes received no answer and cannot establish that the ONUs are offline.
The same no-response result occurs uniformly across the tested PON, while the customer is recorded online, has a current session, and is passing traffic.
The subscriber's current RX power of -19.84 dBm and TX power of 2.29 dBm are normal, with stable seven-day RX, TX, distance, and bias telemetry.
Peers on the port are predominantly online, and the OLT has 174 of 183 ONUs online; the nine offline ONUs are close to normal background levels and do not prove an outage.
The customer has only two sessions in 24 hours with approximately normal duration, and RADIUS, VLAN, and CRM identity data are consistent.
The alarm claims all 7 of 7 PONs failed, but service telemetry and traffic contradict a real OLT-wide outage; therefore the health check itself is the fault.

remediation.action: Repair or reconfigure the SNMP PON/ONU subtree polling for OLT 10.220.57.6, including OID support, credentials, access control, and vendor/MIB compatibility. Suppress or correct the all-PON critical rule when the OLT ping, base SNMP, ONU telemetry, customer sessions, and traffic indicate service is healthy. Re-run the PON probe after correction and separately investigate the normal-background offline ONU count without declaring an outage.

ground_truth.root_cause: The OLT firmware (V2.04.12R) does not expose the ONU parameter OID subtree the health check reads. Every sampled ONU returns no instance, the check marks all seven PONs failed and writes a critical status, while the OLT and all 183 customers are operating normally.
expected_reasoning: Health check reports critical with all 7 of 7 PONs failed
OLT ping succeeds and SNMP sysUpTime answers, with 61 days of uptime and no recent reboot
OLT CPU 22%, memory 19% and temperature 44C are all at healthy baseline
Live probe returns oid_subtree_responds false, and every ONU on the port returns responds false rather than online 0
Uniform non-response means nothing answered; it is not a definite negative, so no ONU has been reported down
CRM shows 174 of 183 ONUs online, and 9 offline matches the 4.85% network baseline
The representative customer holds a session opened 14 hours ago and is passing normal daily traffic
Cached optical readings are 22 minutes old and normal, and telemetry has been flat for seven days
Healthy service with uniform probe non-response indicates an OID or firmware mismatch in the monitoring tool, not a network outage

expected_escalation.review_reason: Health check produces false criticals on firmware V2.04.12R; the OID subtree it reads is absent on this version

distractors: The critical alarm invites an olt_failure or pon_port_failure diagnosis
Nine genuinely offline ONUs on the OLT are unrelated background noise at the normal rate
Firmware V2.04.12R differs from the estate norm V2.03.78R, which is the discriminator rather than a fault in itself
